# dotnet-10-performance-suite

Source: https://github.com/garyciampa/dotnet10performancesuite/blob/master/README.md

# dotnet-10-performance-suite


This repository contains small samples and benchmarks demonstrating performance improvements and modern patterns in .NET 10. The code is inspired by the Microsoft blog post: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/performance-improvements-in-net-10/

![StringConcat comparison](results/stringconcat-comparison.svg)

## Structure

- `src/PerfSamples`: class library with small sample implementations (loop vs LINQ, string concat idioms, JSON serialization examples, ArrayPool usage).
- `src/PerfDemo`: console app that runs short demos and prints timings for quick validation.
- `src/PerfBenchmarks`: BenchmarkDotNet project with microbenchmarks to measure differences. Benchmark results are written to `src/PerfBenchmarks/BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/results/`.

## Prerequisites

- .NET 10 SDK installed (preview/RC when applicable). Verify with `dotnet --version`.
- For consistent benchmark results, run on a machine with minimal background activity and with power plan set to "High performance" (BenchmarkDotNet may adjust this automatically).

## How to build and run

1. Restore and build (Release recommended for benchmarks):
   ```powershell
   dotnet restore
   dotnet build -c Release
   ```

2. Run the demo (quick validation):
   ```powershell
   dotnet run --project src/PerfDemo/PerfDemo.csproj -c Release
   ```

3. Run all benchmarks (this will take several minutes):
   ```powershell
   dotnet run -c Release --project src/PerfBenchmarks/PerfBenchmarks.csproj
   ```

4. Run a single benchmark (use `--filter` with a wildcard):
   ```powershell
   dotnet run -c Release --project src/PerfBenchmarks/PerfBenchmarks.csproj -- --filter "*PoolBenchmarks*"
   ```

### Building for a specific framework

The projects in this repository now multi-target `net9.0` and `net10.0`. To build or run for a specific framework, pass the `-f` / `--framework` option to the CLI or use the `-p:TargetFramework` MSBuild property. Examples:

```powershell
# Build for .NET 9
dotnet build -c Release -f net9.0

# Run the demo for .NET 9
dotnet run -c Release -f net9.0 --project src/PerfDemo/PerfDemo.csproj

# Run benchmarks for .NET 9
dotnet run -c Release -f net9.0 --project src/PerfBenchmarks/PerfBenchmarks.csproj -- --filter "*PoolBenchmarks*"

# Build for .NET 10
dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0
```

Notes:
- If you omit `-f`, the SDK will build all target frameworks by default (multi-targeting); that may increase build time.
- Use framework-specific runs when comparing results across different runtimes or SDKs.

## Benchmark best practices (annotations)

- Always run benchmarks in `Release` mode with no debugger attached.
- Isolate the machine as much as possible: close unneeded apps and network-heavy services.
- Prefer running benchmarks multiple times at different times of day and average results.
- Keep `BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/` in `.gitignore` (this repo already ignores them). If you want to store a reproducible snapshot, export the generated HTML/CSV files to a separate `results/` directory and commit only those files (or attach them to a release), not the entire `BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/` folder.
- Use `--filter` to target specific benchmarks when iterating on a change.
- When comparing across runtimes or SDKs, pin the exact SDK version used and record it in the results (BenchmarkDotNet includes runtime and SDK information in the reports).

## Interpreting results

- BenchmarkDotNet exports detailed reports in HTML and CSV under `src/PerfBenchmarks/BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/results/`.
- Use the generated HTML for human-readable reports and CSV for automated processing or graphs.
- Memory diagnostics are included when `[MemoryDiagnoser]` is used on benchmark classes; check the `Allocated` column for per-op allocations.

**Single-benchmark summary**: a concise HTML summary for the StringConcat benchmark run on .NET 10 has been generated at `results/stringconcat-net10-summary.html`. Use this file for a quick human-readable snapshot of the mean per-op times and allocations for `ConcatUsingPlus`, `ConcatUsingStringBuilder`, and `ConcatUsingStringCreate`.

## CI guidance

- In CI, avoid running full BenchmarkDotNet reports on every push — prefer running them on scheduled runs or when preparing a release; they are time-consuming and environment-sensitive.
- Use CI to build and run unit tests; if you need to run benchmarks in CI, run a smaller subset and publish the resulting HTML/CSV to build artifacts.

## CI notes:

- The GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) now builds both `net9.0` and `net10.0` by default (matrix). That means pushes and PRs will run builds for both targets.
- You can manually trigger the workflow from the Actions tab and select the `framework` input (`all`, `net9.0`, or `net10.0`) to run only one target.
- The workflow includes an optional `benchmarks` job that is only enabled for manual dispatch (and only for `net10.0` by default); this prevents slow benchmark runs from running on every push.

## Contribution & license

Contributions welcome. Open issues or PRs for new samples or benchmark scenarios.

License: MIT — see `LICENSE` file.

# Contributing to dotnet-10-performance-suite

Source: https://github.com/garyciampa/dotnet10performancesuite/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to dotnet-10-performance-suite

Thanks for your interest in contributing — contributions are welcome.

How to contribute

1. Fork the repository and create a feature branch named using the pattern `feat/<short-description>` or `fix/<short-description>`.
2. Keep changes focused and small. Open separate PRs for independent changes.
3. Include tests where applicable and ensure the solution builds for the supported target frameworks:
   - `dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0`
   - `dotnet build -c Release -f net9.0`
4. Run unit tests (if added):
   - `dotnet test --configuration Release`
5. For performance-related changes: include BenchmarkDotNet results showing baseline and your changes. Use the built-in benchmarks in `src/PerfBenchmarks` and prefer running targeted benchmarks with `--filter`.

Code style and quality

- Format code with `dotnet format` before committing.
- Keep public APIs stable; document breaking changes in the PR description.
- Add XML doc comments for public APIs.

Submitting a pull request

- Rebase or merge the latest `main` (or target branch) before opening the PR.
- Provide a clear description and motivation for the change.
- For performance changes, include a short summary of benchmark results and the commands used to produce them.

Issue reporting

- If you find a bug, open an issue with a minimal reproduction, environment details (OS, .NET SDK version), and steps to reproduce.

Thank you for helping improve this project!

# Release notes — v0.1.0

Source: https://github.com/garyciampa/dotnet10performancesuite/blob/master/release-notes.md

# Release notes — v0.1.0

## StringConcat benchmarks — .NET 9 vs .NET 10 (summary)

Environment
- Host: Windows 11, Intel Core i7-11370H 3.30GHz
- Benchmark framework: BenchmarkDotNet v0.15.2
- Runtimes:
  - .NET 9 runtime: 9.0.9
  - .NET 10 runtime: 10.0.0 (10.0.25.45207)

Summary table (mean per-op time)

| Method | .NET 9 (mean) | .NET 10 (mean) | Change | % faster (.NET 10 vs .NET 9) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ConcatUsingPlus | 13.856 ns | 12.177 ns | -1.679 ns | 12.1% |
| ConcatUsingStringBuilder | 60.188 ns | 45.392 ns | -14.796 ns | 24.6% |
| ConcatUsingStringCreate | 15.216 ns | 13.138 ns | -2.078 ns | 13.7% |

Allocations per operation (managed)
- ConcatUsingPlus: 64 B (both runtimes)
- ConcatUsingStringBuilder: 272 B (both runtimes)
- ConcatUsingStringCreate: 64 B (both runtimes)

Notes
- The .NET 10 runtime shows consistent improvements across the string-concatenation idioms measured here. The largest improvement is observed for the `StringBuilder` approach (~24.6% mean time reduction).
- These results are a single snapshot for the host and SDK versions listed above. For rigorous conclusions, repeat runs on multiple machines and aggregate results.

Reproducibility
- Full, detailed BenchmarkDotNet reports (CSV/HTML) are available in the repository under `src/PerfBenchmarks/BenchmarkDotNet.Artifacts/results/` and the release assets.
- To reproduce locally:
  - Build: `dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0` and/or `-f net9.0`
  - Run the string-concat benchmarks: `dotnet run -c Release --project src/PerfBenchmarks/PerfBenchmarks.csproj -- --filter "*StringConcatBenchmarks*"`

# Security policy

Source: https://github.com/garyciampa/dotnet10performancesuite/blob/master/SECURITY.md

# Security policy

If you discover a security vulnerability in this repository, please report it privately so the maintainers can respond and remediate it.

Recommended reporting channels

- Use GitHub Security Advisories (preferred) by going to the repository "Security" tab and opening a private advisory.
- If you cannot use Security Advisories, email a report to `security@your-domain.example` (replace with a real contact address) including:
  - A short title and description of the issue
  - Reproduction steps and minimally reproducible sample
  - A suggested mitigation or fix, if available

Please do not open public issues describing unpatched security vulnerabilities.

Response expectations

Maintainers will acknowledge the report and provide an estimated timeline for a fix. Once fixed, maintainers will coordinate a disclosure timeline and publish an advisory.
